But the citation names an edition nobody read. Gutenberg #1184 names no translator and no source edition, and its spelling is American ('opal-colored'), which a London Chapman and Hall printing of 1846 would not use. The anonymous translation also appears in different wordings in different printings. The Routledge five-volume edition (London and New York, 1888, copyright 1887 by J. L. Blamire; archive.org countofmontecris05dumauoft, vol. V, chapter CXVIII, about p. 263) reads: 'Live, then, and be happy, beloved children of my heart! and never forget, that until the day when God will deign to reveal the future to man, all human wisdom is contained in these two words,— ‘Wait and hope.’' That printing has 'will' for 'shall' and 'contained' for 'summed up', and it ends the paragraph before with 'enjoyments of life' where Gutenberg has 'of living'. So this translation's wording varies between printings, and nothing shows that the Gutenberg wording is what Chapman and Hall printed in 1846. The archive.org scan of Chapman and Hall 1846 vol. II (countmontecrist03dumagoog) has no text layer, so I could not settle the question. As cited, this is a confident citation to an edition whose wording is unconfirmed, and that is the failure this track exists to prevent. To fix it, read the letter in the Chapman and Hall 1846 vol. II page images and ship that wording, or cite an edition that is actually named and whose text has been read.
